title: Model Substitutability Index + Buyers' Journey Mapping
creator: Asha Menon
description: Build a repeatable Model Substitutability Index (MSI) that quantifies how easily a customer can switch between models/providers for a given workload, and map typical buyers' journeys and friction points when migrating models. Deliverables: MSI scoring rubric, dataset of model signals, buyer journey archetypes, and a visualization for PM/GTMs to prioritize competitive playbooks.
background: Sales and Solutions teams report an uptick in RFPs where customers evaluate multiple open models and managed inference providers; we lack a unified metric that captures technical compatibility (APIs, latency/cost parity, output fidelity), procurement frictions (licenses, IP), and operational migration effort (KV cache, quantization, infra). This ticket synthesizes market signals, customer interviews, and internal telemetry to create a prioritization tool for product roadmaps and GTM.
success_metrics: MSI computed for 50+ popular model variants across 6 vertical workload archetypes
Three buyer journey archetypes documented with pain points and decision triggers
Launch of a lightweight dashboard in Confluence + one-pager GTM playbook
At least two prioritized product actions (routing policy, compatibility shim) validated with Solutions team
acceptance_criteria: MSI rubric reviewed and approved by Eng (runtime) and Research teams
Data sources defined and ingest scripts documented in PRD/link to GitHub (or mock data if access pending)
Buyer journey artifacts include interview notes (5 customers/prospects) and sales win/loss analysis
Dashboard prototype accessible to PM and Sales; roadmap items created for follow-up work
updates: 2026-02-25: Ticket created; initial scoping with Solutions and Research. Decided to focus first on embedding and chat-generation workloads as high-signal verticals.

2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng runtime to identify telemetry signals we can surface (latency percentiles per sequence length, quantization compatibility flags, KV migration effort estimates). Eng requested a narrowed feature list for MVP.
2026-03-06: Conducted 3 customer discovery calls (two fintech, one healthcare). Early signal: procurement license mismatch and support SLAs are top non-technical blockers.
2026-03-09: Draft MSI rubric v0.1 posted to Confluence; Design sketched dashboard wireframes. Feedback from Research: add hallucination/regression sensitivity as a factor for chat workloads.
2026-03-12: Meeting with GTM to align on playbooks; agreed to produce one-pager actions: (1) routing fallback policy for high-MSI customers, (2) compatibility shim checklist for Solutions onboarding.

2026-03-14: Blocker noted: lack of normalized inference cost metrics across managed providers. Action - PM to request anonymized cost buckets from Finance; can proceed with relative-cost proxies if delayed.
